dataset.name: Leaf gas exchange survey by leaf age, Feb2017, PA-SLZ: Panama
description: Leaf gas exchange survey measurements on in situ sunlit canopy leaves of four tree species from the San Lorenzo Canopy Crane Site in Panama in February 2017. Multiple measurements were taken on young, mature and old leaves at 3 or 4 time points for each species (early morning, mid-morning, solar noon, afternoon) over 4 days. This data was collected as part of the 2017 BNL–STRI leaf traits by age campaign. See related datasets for other measurements made as part of this campaign including leaf water potential, leaf spectra, sap flow, leaf mass per area, other gas exchange measurements and leaf chemistry.Note: A corrected version of the data file was posted on October 9, 2018.
This dataset was originally published on the NGEE Tropics Archive and is being mirrored on ESS-DIVE for long-term archival

Acknowledgement: This research was supported as part of NGEE-Tropics, funded by the U.S. Department of Energy, Office of Science, Office of Biological and Environmental Research under contract no. DE-SC0012704

spatialCoverage.description: Site Name: Bosque Protector San Lorenzo (Fort Sherman). Site ID: PA-SLZ. Located in Panama. Established in 1997, the FTS canopy crane is located approximately 11km South West from the city of Colon, in the middle theParque Natural San Lorenzo (formerly known as FortSherman) and is surrounded by 300-year old, low-landtropical rainforest. The crane is 52 meters tall with aradius of 54 meters, and can reach approximately 240species of trees and lianas. (Paton 2015 FTS Met report) For more information on this site, visit: http://biogeodb.stri.si.edu/physical_monitoring/research/sherman,http://www.stri.si.edu/english/research/facilities/terrestrial/cranes/cranes_and_sites.php Site contact(s): (Argelis Ruiz <ruiza@si.edu>)

measurementTechnique: Corrections made as required per logged remarks and notebook entries. QC column in datafile flags log points considered bad data. Bad data is attributed to failure to reach stable conditions in the leaf chamber, or rates below detection. Any result with negative A, Ci or conductance is flagged as bad data. See included pdf for a full description of the survey gas exchange methods.
